from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Conditional probability: P(A|B) narrows our universe.", "Consider our total sample space, S.", "Subset B acts as our new reality.", "The intersection represents occurrences of A given B.", "Example: Orange animal reduces our animal cage set."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability & Visual Logic", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        formula = MathTex(r"P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}", font_size=36)
        
        venn = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1),
            Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3).shift(LEFT * 0.5),
            Circle(radius=0.8, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.3).shift(RIGHT * 0.5)
        )
        intersection = Intersection(venn[1], venn[2], color="#ADD8E6", fill_opacity=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(formula), run_time=1)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_in_area(venn, 'C2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(venn), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(intersection), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#ADD8E6")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        inter_label = MathTex(r"P(A \cap B)", color="#FFFFE0", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(inter_label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Flash(inter_label), FadeIn(inter_label), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFE0")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        note = Text("Evidence changes our belief", font_size=20, color="#F0F8FF")
        self.place_at_grid(note, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(note), run_time=1)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#F0F8FF")

        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Independence: The 'No Influence' Condition", [
            "- Independence: Knowing B provides zero info about A.",
            "- Mathematically, this means P(A|B) equals P(A).",
            "- Imagine a coin flip and a spinning wheel."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        circle_a = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        circle_b = Circle(radius=0.8, color=YELLOW).set_fill(YELLOW, opacity=0.3)
        
        self.place_at_grid(circle_a, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(circle_b, "B5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(circle_a), FadeIn(circle_b))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        equation = MathTex(r"P(A|B) = P(A)", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(equation, "D2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # B moves without changing A's size to show independence
        target_pos = self.grid["D5"]
        self.play(
            circle_b.animate.move_to(target_pos),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "Bayes' Theorem: Reversing the logic of evidence.",
            "We calculate P(A|B) using the likelihood.",
            "It connects P(B|A) back to our original prior.",
            "This updates our belief with new data.",
            "Crucial for real-world smart device accuracy."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reversing Evidence", lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        formula = MathTex("P(A|B) = \\frac{P(B|A) \\cdot P(A)}{P(B)}", font_size=48)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B1', 'C6')
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        p_b_a = formula[0][8:13] # Isolating P(B|A)
        self.play(p_b_a.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid['C3'], end=self.grid['B3'], color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        p_b = formula[0][16:19] # Isolating P(B)
        self.play(Indicate(p_b, color=PINK))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(PINK)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Representing a balance scale icon
        scale_icon = VGroup(
            Line(LEFT, RIGHT),
            Line(ORIGIN, UP),
            Dot(LEFT*0.5 + DOWN*0.2),
            Dot(RIGHT*0.5 + DOWN*0.2)
        ).set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(scale_icon, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(scale_icon))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(BLUE)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis & Real-world Application", [
            "Synthesizing: Prior, Evidence, and Posterior probability.", 
            "Bayes' updates certainty in the face of uncertainty.", 
            "Testing example: Prior prevalence informs posterior diagnosis."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Fade in text 'Medical Diagnosis Example' in white #FFFFFF.
        header = Text("Medical Diagnosis Example", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(header, 'A1', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(header))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display test sensitivity and false positive rates.
        data = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"P(\text{Pos}|\text{Sick}) = 0.95", color="#FFD700"),
            MathTex(r"P(\text{Pos}|\text{Healthy}) = 0.05", color="#FF7F50")
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT)
        self.place_in_area(data, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(data))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate final probability calculation with bold result #00FF00.
        result = MathTex(r"P(\text{Sick}|\text{Pos}) \approx 0.16", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(result, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Create(result))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#87CEEB"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability & Visual Logic
sections.content: Define conditional probability P(A|B) as the probability of A occurring given that B has already occurred. Introduce the 'Subset Logic' visual: A Venn diagram showing total sample space S, event B as a circle, and the overlap with A representing P(A∩B).
sections.example: In a cage of 10 animals, 6 are cats and 4 are dogs. If we pick an animal that is 'orange', how does our sample space shrink to only the orange animals?

sections.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Condition
sections.content: Define independence: Events A and B are independent if P(A|B) = P(A). Visually demonstrate this using a 'Flip and Spin' animation: A coin flip does not change the probability of a spinner landing on red. If they are independent, the knowledge of B provides zero information about A.
sections.example: Flipping a coin (Heads) and rolling a six-sided die (Six). Knowing the coin is heads does not change the probability of rolling a six.

sections.title: Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reversing Evidence
sections.content: Introduce the formula P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Use an 'Inversion Animation' to show how we move from 'Likelihood of the evidence' to 'Probability of the cause'. Highlight that this is essential for updating beliefs based on new data.
sections.example: A smart camera (Device) detects a cat. Given the camera has a 90% accuracy rate (P(B|A)), what is the actual probability that the object is a cat given the alarm sounded?

sections.title: Synthesis & Real-world Application
sections.content: Connect the concepts: Check if evidence is independent to simplify complex calculations. Summarize Bayes' Theorem as a tool for logical updating in the face of uncertainty. End with a visual flow chart connecting Prior Probability -> New Evidence -> Posterior Probability.
sections.example: Medical testing: Using a prior probability (disease prevalence) and a test result (evidence) to calculate the posterior probability of a patient having a specific condition.
